item.title: NEW: Maersk Confirms Breach; WhiteArmor Ransomware Demands $5M Ransom
item.description:
Headline: Maersk Confirms Breach; WhiteArmor Ransomware Demands $5M Ransom

Summary:
Global shipping firm Maersk has confirmed a data breach affecting a legacy IT system from a previous acquisition. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims to have stolen 100GB of sensitive logistics data, including plaintext passwords and customer records, and is demanding a $5 million ransom. Maersk states the incident is isolated and does not anticipate disruption to customer operations, though the attackers have published detailed lists of allegedly stolen data to apply pressure.

item.description:
Headline: Microsoft's Record Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Including Outlook Zero-Day

Summary:
Microsoft has released its November 2026 Patch Tuesday update, addressing a record-breaking 1,235 vulnerabilities across its products. The most critical fix is for CVE-2026-124194, an actively exploited zero-day spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes with a single click from a victim, bypassing security warnings. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating a patch for federal agencies by November 24.

Severity: Critical

The malware is designed to run within GitHub Actions to exfiltrate sensitive CI/CD secrets, including repository secrets, cloud credentials, and API keys, posing a severe threat to software development and deployment pipelines.

item.title: NEW: Microsoft Reveals 'Lazarus,' a Stealthy AI Supply Chain Attack
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft Reveals 'Lazarus,' a Stealthy AI Supply Chain Attack

Summary:
Microsoft researchers have disclosed 'Lazarus,' a novel and highly stealthy AI supply-chain attack technique. The method allows an attacker to surgically backdoor open-weight large language models (LLMs) by modifying fewer than ten dormant neurons. This nearly undetectable edit, which requires no model retraining, can be activated by a secret trigger in a prompt, forcing the AI agent to execute arbitrary commands using its assigned privileges. The research highlights a critical new threat vector for the rapidly growing field of agentic AI.

Severity: High

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Threat Intelligence, Cloud Security

Article Type: Analysis

Meta Description: Microsoft researchers disclose 'Lazarus,' a new AI supply chain attack that can surgically backdoor large language models by modifying a few neurons.

item.title: NEW: Falcon C2 Framework Compromises Browsers to Target Governments
item.description:
Headline: Falcon C2 Framework Compromises Browsers to Target Governments

Summary:
Unit 42 has identified a browser-based command and control (C2) framework named Falcon (also known as XG or Xiàng Gē). The threat actor leverages this framework to compromise government webmail portals and applications by injecting malicious JavaScript. Operating entirely within the browser, Falcon can sideload malicious Chrome extensions and exfiltrate sensitive information. The campaign, observed between March and May 2026, targeted government ministries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. The framework also serves as a delivery mechanism for a secondary implant called Antino, which uses Microsoft OneDrive for C2 communications. Analysis reveals a high-confidence link between Falcon and the PeckBirdy framework previously reported by Trend Micro.

Severity: High

Categories: Malware, Threat Actor, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Report

Reading Time: 24 minutes

Meta Description: Unit 42 analysis of Falcon (XG), a browser-based C2 framework used to compromise government web portals and exfiltrate data via malicious JavaScript and browser extensions.

item.title: UPDATE: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms
item.description:
Headline: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms

Summary:
A coordinated wave of attacks dubbed "Black October" has compromised at least nine AI developer platforms, including Northflank, Railway, and Lightning AI. Security researchers at Wiz, who identified the campaign, report that attackers targeted environment variables to steal API keys and other secrets. This technique, termed "LLMJacking," allows threat actors to hijack expensive AI model services for their own use, leading to significant fraudulent charges for victims. Northflank confirmed the breach after being alerted by Wiz, noting that multiple customers had reported unauthorized use of their AI API keys. The campaign highlights a critical credential crisis in AI infrastructure, with some attacks employing "agent swarm" tactics and resulting in at least one platform, Zeabur, shutting down permanently.

Severity: High

Categories: Cyberattack, Cloud Security, Data Breach

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: A coordinated attack wave in October 2026, dubbed 'Black October,' compromised nine AI developer platforms to steal API keys for a new resource hijacking technique called 'LLMJacking.'

item.description:
Headline: Microsoft Patches Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day in Massive Update

Summary:
Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed over 1,200 vulnerabilities, including a critical zero-day in Outlook, CVE-2026-124194, which is being actively exploited. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes by tricking users into opening a malicious message file. The vulnerability does not trigger in the Preview Pane, requiring direct user interaction. In response, CISA has added CVE-2026-124194 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch by November 24, 2026.

item.description:
Headline: France Blames Iran-Backed Group for Sabotaging 700+ Supermarket Refrigerators

Summary:
French and U.S. authorities have attributed a large-scale sabotage campaign against over 700 European supermarkets to SHAHID KAVEH, an Iranian state-backed group affiliated with the IRGC. The attackers remotely compromised and manipulated industrial refrigeration controllers, causing tens of millions of euros in damages from food spoilage and equipment fires. The attacks exploited exposed web interfaces on controllers from brands like Danfoss and Copeland. France has condemned the incident as a destructive act of sabotage and is pursuing EU-level sanctions.

Headline: N-able Takes N-central RMM Offline After 30+ Zero-Days Publicly Disclosed

Summary:
IT software provider N-able was forced to take its hosted N-central RMM platform offline globally after a security researcher publicly disclosed over 30 zero-day vulnerabilities, dubbed 'Able2Shell.' The flaws, which include critical bugs leading to unauthenticated remote code execution, were published with proof-of-concept exploits. N-able has since released an emergency hotfix, 2026.4 HF2, and is advising all on-premises customers to patch immediately due to the severe supply chain risk posed to managed service providers (MSPs).

item.description:
Headline: Blind Eagle APT Uses HTML Smuggling to Target Latin American Entities

Summary:
The Spanish-speaking APT group Blind Eagle (APT-C-36) has launched a new espionage campaign targeting government, judicial, and financial entities in Latin America, with a focus on Colombia. The operation uses sophisticated spear-phishing emails with judicial themes that employ HTML smuggling to deliver a malicious ZIP archive, bypassing email security gateways. The final payload is a custom remote access trojan (RAT), derived from AsyncRAT, capable of data exfiltration and keystroke logging.
